question: Why is self-medication so common across Nigeria?

options.A: Standard hospitals rarely stock basic pain relief tablets
options.B: People prefer reading package leaflets over talking to doctors
options.C: Hospital queues, costs, and easy access to open-air drug markets drive the practice
options.D: The government mandates that every citizen treat themselves first

explanation: You got it! Long wait times at clinics and financial constraints often push people to easily accessible informal drug vendors instead. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h1)

question: Besides antibodies, what specific viral marker do fourth-generation HIV tests look for?

options.A: p24 antigen
options.B: Integrase enzyme
options.C: Reverse transcriptase
options.D: gp120 protein

explanation: Awesome work! Fourth-gen tests search for the p24 antigen alongside antibodies, helping us catch recent infections much earlier. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which psychological challenge is most common in young brides facing severe isolation and abuse?

options.A: Seasonal affective syndrome
options.B: Depression and anxiety
options.C: Bipolar manic disorder
options.D: Paranoid personality disorder

explanation: Spot on! The heavy trauma, loneliness, and lack of freedom often push young brides into deep depression and anxiety. Mental health care is part of our nursing duty. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which heart chamber is most frequently injured in penetrating chest trauma due to its front-facing position?

options.A: Left atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Right atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The right ventricle sits directly behind the sternum, making it the most exposed and frequently injured chamber when sharp or high-speed objects penetrate the chest. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h2)

question: What kind of skin graft uses skin taken from another part of the patient's own body?

options.A: Xenograft
options.B: Autograft
options.C: Heterograft
options.D: Allograft

explanation: Auto means self! An autograft uses the patient's own skin so their body won't reject it. Smart healing science! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason we preserve food?

options.A: To completely eliminate all vitamins from food items
options.B: To replace natural food colors with artificial dyes
options.C: To stop or slow down food spoilage and microbial growth
options.D: To make food taste significantly sweeter and saltier

explanation: Food preservation stops germs and chemical reactions from spoiling our meals, helping keep food safe to eat later! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h1)

question: What percentage of nephrons in the human kidney are classified as cortical nephrons?

options.A: About 50 percent
options.B: About 99 percent
options.C: About 85 percent
options.D: About 15 percent

explanation: The vast majority of nephrons in a healthy human kidney are cortical nephrons located mostly in the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why does the body rely on both innate and adaptive defenses?

options.A: Innate destroys viruses while adaptive only handles bacterial infections
options.B: Innate immunity creates antibodies while adaptive creates physical barriers
options.C: Adaptive defense works entirely independently of the innate system
options.D: Innate provides immediate defense while adaptive targets specific invaders later

explanation: Spot on! Innate immunity jumps in instantly to buy time, while the adaptive system gears up to launch a precise, targeted attack. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h1)

question: An EPS report shows dangerous heart rhythms that couldn't be fixed with ablation. What might the medical team look at next?

options.A: Preparing the patient for discussion about an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
options.B: Removing all cardiac monitoring equipment permanently
options.C: Scheduling an immediate open-heart surgery for valve replacement
options.D: Discharging the patient with no further restrictions or medications

explanation: When an abnormal pathway can't be successfully ablated away, an implantable device (like an ICD) is often the next line of defense to keep the patient safe from sudden cardiac arrest. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h6)

question: When a blood vessel gets injured, what is the correct order of the steps your body takes to stop bleeding?

options.A: Coagulation, vascular spasm, platelet plug formation
options.B: Platelet plug formation, coagulation, vascular spasm
options.C: Vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, coagulation
options.D: Coagulation, fibrinolysis, vascular spasm

explanation: Great thinking! First, the vessel squeezes tight (spasm), then platelets rush in to patch the hole (plug), and finally, the clotting proteins seal it up solid (coagulation). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h6)

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of an infective host?

options.A: To act exclusively as a dead-end for microbial life
options.B: To harbor an infectious agent and serve as a source of infection
options.C: To manufacture antibodies for community protection
options.D: To destroy invading pathogens before symptoms appear

explanation: You've got this! Think of the host as a comfortable home for the germ. It gives the pathogen a place to stay and acts as the starting point for spreading to others. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does bladder retraining help a patient with urge incontinence?

options.A: It numbs the bladder nerves permanently using special exercises
options.B: It trains the bladder to hold increasing amounts of urine by voiding on a set timetable
options.C: It empties the bladder continuously so the patient never feels any sensation
options.D: It stops the kidneys from producing urine during the night hours

explanation: Following a set bathroom schedule helps calm the bladder down and slowly helps it hold more urine over time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h6)

question: Oh no—you accidentally experience a needle-stick injury while in a patient's home. What is your very first move?

options.A: Call the local police department to file an accident report
options.B: Finish the remaining nursing tasks for that client visit
options.C: Squeeze the puncture wound hard to force out trapped blood
options.D: Wash the exposed skin thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: Safety first! Always wash the area right away with soap and water to wash away surface germs before doing anything else. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h8)

question: How does cutting back on coffee and energy drinks help a patient dealing with an anxiety disorder?

options.A: It prevents central nervous system stimulation that mimics anxiety symptoms
options.B: It guarantees uninterrupted sleep for twelve hours every night
options.C: It acts as a powerful direct replacement for antidepressant medication
options.D: It cures the genetic predisposition linked to panic disorder

explanation: Correct! Caffeine is a stimulant that causes jitteriness and a fast pulse—things you definitely don't need when managing anxiety. Smart choice! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do pregnant women routinely need iron supplements during gestation?

options.A: To harden the bones of the mother's hands and feet
options.B: To increase the amount of amniotic fluid in the womb
options.C: To support the significant increase in maternal blood volume
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! A pregnant woman's body makes a lot more blood to support the baby, and iron helps prevent anemia during this heavy workload. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h4)

question: What happens to the heart muscle fibers during Ventricular Fibrillation?

options.A: They beat together in a slow, steady rhythm
options.B: They rest without any electrical signals at all
options.C: They become completely stiff and cannot relax
options.D: They twitch randomly without pumping any blood

explanation: During VF, the heart muscle fibers flutter and twitch chaotically like a bag of worms. Because they aren't working together, no blood is pumped to the body. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h2)

question: Why do doctors give antibiotics along with fluids when treating cholera?

options.A: To completely replace the need for drinking water
options.B: To rebuild the muscular lining of the stomach
options.C: To shorten illness duration and reduce bacteria shedding
options.D: To prevent the spread of mosquito vectors

explanation: Antibiotics aren't the main fix (fluids are!), but they help clear the bacteria faster so the patient recovers sooner. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T18#GNS313_U2_T18_h5)

question: How does a hospital growing much larger usually affect its organisational design?

options.A: It eliminates all need for formal chains of command
options.B: It forces the organisation to become completely boundaryless
options.C: It automatically shrinks the span of control for every worker
options.D: It tends to make the organisation more mechanistic with more rules

explanation: As a hospital grows bigger, it usually adds more departments, layers, and rules to keep things organized and under control. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main goal when treating a patient with a peptic ulcer?

options.A: Heal the ulcer and relieve pain
options.B: Permanently stop all food digestion
options.C: Increase stomach acid production
options.D: Remove the entire stomach lining

explanation: We want to help the stomach sore heal up so the patient feels comfortable again and doesn't keep getting painful flare-ups! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the hallmark sign of tardive dyskinesia?

options.A: Involuntary, rhythmic movements of the tongue and jaw
options.B: A complete inability to produce spoken words
options.C: An overwhelming and uncomfortable inner restlessness
options.D: Sudden painful spasms of the neck muscles

explanation: Tardive dyskinesia involves late-appearing, repetitive movements—like lip-smacking, tongue darting, or chewing motions—that the patient cannot control. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why is it important to report research findings back to the community where a study took place?

options.A: It prevents community members from asking questions about the budget
options.B: It ensures the researchers receive financial bonuses from donors
options.C: It is required by law before any doctor can write a prescription
options.D: It builds mutual trust and respects the participants who gave their time

explanation: Returning results to the community honors participants and fosters cooperative relationships for future health projects. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why are stool softeners commonly prescribed after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To increase the speed of food digestion in the stomach
options.B: To prevent straining that can disrupt the suture line
options.C: To increase blood flow to the lower limbs
options.D: To cure chronic urinary tract infections

explanation: Avoiding hard stools and straining protects the delicate surgical repairs from tension and tearing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What happens to a mother's body when her diet lacks proper nutrition during pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood volume increases beyond normal limits
options.B: The fetus draws nutrients from the mother's own body stores
options.C: Fetal growth remains completely unaffected by maternal diet
options.D: The placenta stops growing completely to save energy

explanation: When food intake is low, the clever baby takes what it needs from your own body reserves! This is why mums can feel so drained. You're doing great learning how the body adapts. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h1)

question: A patient complains of frequent hard stools and infrequent bowel movements. What is your best first piece of advice?

options.A: Eliminate all physical activity to rest the bowel
options.B: Stop eating all solid foods for forty-eight hours
options.C: Take strong prescription laxatives every morning
options.D: Increase daily water intake and eat more fiber-rich foods

explanation: Fluids and fiber are always the safest, most natural starting point to help a patient beat simple constipation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h3)

question: A patient treated for a wasp sting allergy feels fine after 30 minutes and wants to go home. What should you tell them?

options.A: Explain that the patient must stay longer because a secondary reaction can happen hours later
options.B: Tell the patient that once symptoms stop, they will never have another reaction
options.C: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to be completely safe before leaving
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines

explanation: Allergic reactions can strike twice! We call this a biphasic reaction, meaning the patient needs to stick around for observation just in case symptoms return hours later. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h6)

question: An increasing population of older adults in Nigeria will most likely lead to a higher demand for what service?

options.A: Management of chronic health conditions
options.B: Primary school infrastructure
options.C: Pediatric immunizations and infant care
options.D: Obstetric and maternity wards

explanation: Older populations experience higher rates of long-term illnesses like high blood pressure and diabetes, increasing the need for chronic care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the most likely cause when fluid leaks constantly around the outside of a drainage tube?

options.A: Normal healing of the deeper muscle layers inside
options.B: The collection bag hanging below the level of the bed
options.C: The patient drinking too much water during the night
options.D: A loose seal or saturation of the current dressing

explanation: Leakage around the tube entry site often happens when the dressing is too full to hold more fluid or when the seal around the tube is compromised. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks presents with a severe headache, blurred vision, and high blood pressure. What condition should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Pre-eclampsia
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: High blood pressure combined with visual disturbances and severe headaches during pregnancy are classic warning signs of pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h2)

question: Why must quality assurance decisions be data-driven rather than based on guesswork?

options.A: Data collection completely eliminates all human error
options.B: Data provides accurate proof of where problems exist and if changes actually work
options.C: Hospital management only accepts reports written in numbers
options.D: Guesswork is illegal for registered nurses in Nigeria

explanation: In nursing, we rely on facts! Real data gives us clear proof of what's going wrong and whether our new ideas are actually fixing the problem. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal of a nursing assessment during the menopausal transition?

options.A: To prescribe hormone replacement therapy based on lab values
options.B: To halt the aging process and restore ovarian function
options.C: To evaluate symptom severity, overall health risks, and emotional well-being
options.D: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders independently

explanation: As nurses, we look at the whole picture—how symptoms affect her daily life, her health, and her feelings—to give the best support. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h5)

question: Which health challenge do rural communities face most often?

options.A: Long travel times to reach comprehensive healthcare
options.B: High rates of industrial air pollution and overcrowding
options.C: An overabundance of specialized tertiary hospitals
options.D: Excessive noise pollution from heavy urban traffic

explanation: Correct! Distance and poor roads often make getting to a well-equipped hospital a real journey for rural villagers. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why do nurses collect a sputum sample *before* starting the patient on antibiotics?

options.A: To check if the patient is allergic to drugs
options.B: To clear out the airways so they can breathe right away
options.C: To measure the red blood cell count in the airway
options.D: To find the exact germ so the right antibiotic can be given

explanation: Getting the sample first ensures the lab can grow and identify the exact bacteria without antibiotics masking the results. Smart nursing practice! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a main objective of the DRF system?

options.A: Ensuring drug affordability
options.B: Eliminating essential drug stockouts
options.C: Providing free healthcare services to everyone
options.D: Sourcing high-quality medications

explanation: Spot on if you picked free healthcare! DRF drugs are sold at affordable, subsidized rates—not given away for free—so the fund can keep running. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main virus that causes COVID-19?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.B: SARS-CoV-2
options.C: Influenza A virus
options.D: Respiratory Syncytial Virus

explanation: COVID-19 stands for coronavirus disease 2019, and it is caused by the specific virus called Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h1)

question: About how long does one full sleep cycle (moving through NREM and REM stages) last?

options.A: 90 to 110 minutes
options.B: 30 to 45 minutes
options.C: 3 to 4 hours
options.D: 6 to 8 hours

explanation: Your brain cycles through different sleep stages roughly every hour and a half all night long. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h4)

question: Why are transdermal patches unique compared to standard topical creams?

options.A: They deliver a controlled, continuous systemic dose of medication over a long period
options.B: They only work if rubbed vigorously into the dermal layer of the skin
options.C: They are completely water-soluble and wash off easily with light sweat
options.D: They are applied exclusively to open wounds to speed up local cellular healing

explanation: Transdermal patches utilize a special rate-limiting membrane to slowly release medication into the bloodstream over several hours or days. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h3)

question: How should a nurse pull the ear pinna when giving ear drops to an adult patient?

options.A: Downward and forward
options.B: Downward and backward
options.C: Upward and backward
options.D: Straight outward by the lobe

explanation: Pulling the adult ear pinna up and back straightens the curved ear canal so the drops can reach the eardrum area. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is infection control a team duty for all healthcare workers?

options.A: Because cleaning supplies are distributed equally among departments
options.B: Because a single mistake by any staff member can put a patient at risk
options.C: Because only doctors are allowed to handle sterile equipment
options.D: Because hospital management requires daily written reports from nurses

explanation: Spot on! Keeping patients safe is a team effort. Because we all work together around the patient, one small slip by anyone can let germs spread—so every member's vigilance counts. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does the 'impersonal' aspect of the Hot Stove Rule mean?

options.A: Discipline targets the behavior, not the person
options.B: Rules apply only to new nursing staff members
options.C: Managers should never speak to the nurse directly
options.D: Penalties are handed out by a computer program

explanation: Fair discipline focuses purely on what the worker did wrong rather than attacking who they are. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: Which factor directly causes a sudden drop in foetal oxygen due to mechanical compression?

options.A: Umbilical cord prolapse
options.B: Maternal mild anaemia
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Advanced maternal age

explanation: When the umbilical cord slips down before the baby, pressure from the presenting part compresses the cord and immediately blocks blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h2)

question: What is the main job of government policies in healthcare?

options.A: Deciding which patients get admitted to private rooms
options.B: Manufacturing all pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.C: Personally training every nurse and doctor in the country
options.D: Determining service prioritization, funding, and accessibility

explanation: Government policies set the rules for how money is shared and whether health services actually reach the people who need them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of a drug antagonist?

options.A: To block receptors and prevent activation
options.B: To speed up the breakdown of cellular waste
options.C: To mimic hormones and cause a strong response
options.D: To increase the rate of drug absorption

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a stubborn security guard standing in the doorway—it sits on the receptor so nothing else can trigger it. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which symptom during the final months of pregnancy strongly points to placenta previa?

options.A: High fever with foul-smelling amniotic fluid
options.B: Sudden swelling of the feet only
options.C: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding
options.D: Severe painful contractions with a rigid belly

explanation: Well done! Placenta previa happens when the placenta covers the cervix, which typically causes sudden, painless, bright red bleeding. You are mastering your obstetric signs! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to cure viral infections like the common cold?

options.A: Antibiotics are destroyed by stomach acid before reaching viral cells
options.B: Viruses mutate too quickly for white blood cells to recognize them
options.C: Viruses hide inside healthy red blood cells away from medicines
options.D: Viruses do not possess the cellular structures that antibiotics target

explanation: Remember, antibiotics attack bacterial walls or parts that viruses simply don't have. That's why taking antibiotics for a viral flu won't help! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h1)

question: What must happen to qualitative data, like recorded patient interviews, before analysis?

options.A: They must be transcribed word-for-word into written text
options.B: They must be translated into three different foreign languages
options.C: They must be deleted immediately to protect hospital files
options.D: They must be converted entirely into bar charts and graphs

explanation: Audio recordings of interviews need to be written out as text transcripts so researchers can read, code, and analyze the themes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h2)

question: What main technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

options.A: Open-air burning
options.B: High-pressure steam sterilization
options.C: Deep underground freezing
options.D: Chemical dissolution in acid

explanation: Autoclaves use intense steam pressure to hit temperatures that wipe out germs and pathogens on medical items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why would a doctor prescribe the medication sucralfate for a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: It permanently neutralizes all digestive enzymes
options.B: It relaxes the pyloric sphincter to speed up digestion
options.C: It stimulates the pancreas to release more insulin
options.D: It forms a protective coating over the ulcer site

explanation: Great job! Sucralfate acts like a liquid bandage, sticking directly to the ulcer base to shield it from harsh stomach acids and pepsin. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something food safety regulations normally check for?

options.A: Physical objects like metal shards or stones
options.B: Dangerous levels of chemical pesticide residues
options.C: Political views of the food manufacturing company owners
options.D: Harmful germs causing foodborne illnesses

explanation: Food safety is strictly about biological, chemical, and physical hazards—not who owns the company or what they believe! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h5)

question: Who is usually the first member of the nursing team to notice small, daily changes in a resident's condition?

options.A: Director of nursing
options.B: Billing administrator
options.C: Facility pharmacist
options.D: Certified nursing assistant

explanation: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs) spend the most time with residents, making them amazing at spotting early signs of a change in health! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a strong focal point on a health education poster?

options.A: To make the poster look like a modern art painting
options.B: To hide the official logo of the sponsoring health organization
options.C: To immediately draw the viewer's attention to the core health topic
options.D: To use up empty white space at the bottom of the page

explanation: A great focal point grabs the eye instantly, making sure people catch the main health message even if they just glance at it quickly. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main use of calcium carbonate when taken as a mineral supplement?

options.A: Lowering high blood pressure through direct vasodilation
options.B: Neutralizing stomach acid and supporting bone strength
options.C: Stopping acute seizures in pregnant women with eclampsia
options.D: Thinning thick mucus secretions in the respiratory tract

explanation: Calcium carbonate doubles as a handy antacid for the tummy and provides essential calcium to build strong bones! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient develops severe fluid loss following massive burns over 40 percent of their body. Which classification of shock should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Neurogenic shock
options.B: Septic shock
options.C: Hypovolemic shock
options.D: Cardiogenic shock

explanation: Severe burns cause massive plasma loss through damaged skin, leading directly to a shortage of circulating fluid volume. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h3)

question: What should the nurse check when inspecting the dressing after the procedure?

options.A: Whether the skin has turned a pale yellow color
options.B: If the adhesive tape is completely waterproof
options.C: Signs of bleeding, swelling, or fluid leakage
options.D: The exact temperature of the bandage material

explanation: Spot on! Regular site checks ensure any bleeding or fluid leakage is caught and managed early. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'Cluster Approach' in international disaster management?

options.A: To allow military forces to take full command of civilian healthcare facilities
options.B: To group humanitarian organizations by sector to improve coordination and accountability
options.C: To centralize all international financial donations into one bank account
options.D: To ensure that every NGO operates independently without government oversight

explanation: Brilliant! The cluster system groups agencies by their specialty (like health or water) so everyone works together cleanly without overlapping or missing needs. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the medical term for the uterus shrinking back to its normal size after birth?

options.A: Exfoliation
options.B: Lactation
options.C: Autolysis
options.D: Involution

explanation: Great job! Involution is just the word we use for the uterus shrinking back down to its pre-pregnant size. Think of it like a rubber band slowly returning to its original shape. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h2)

question: Which tiny bone in the middle ear is attached directly to the eardrum?

options.A: Incus
options.B: Cochlea
options.C: Stapes
options.D: Malleus

explanation: The malleus (also known as the hammer) rests right against the eardrum to catch its first vibrations. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h3)

question: In a standard 28-day menstrual cycle, around which day does ovulation usually happen?

options.A: Day 14
options.B: Day 28
options.C: Day 7
options.D: Day 21

explanation: Day 14 is the classic midpoint of a 28-day cycle where ovulation takes center stage. Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient needs an allergy drug for daytime use that won't make them sleepy on their heavy-machinery job. Which one is best?

options.A: Promethazine
options.B: Loratadine
options.C: Chlorpheniramine
options.D: Diphenhydramine

explanation: Brilliant choice! Loratadine is a second-generation antihistamine that doesn't cross easily into the brain, keeping your patient alert and safe at work. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h2)

question: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of which common virus is the primary cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Epstein-Barr Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: High-risk types of HPV can cause gradual changes in the cells of the cervix. Over time, these changes can turn cancerous if not caught early by a Pap smear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h5)

question: If a patient is taking Ethambutol, what regular assessment should you prioritize?

options.A: Visual acuity and color discrimination testing
options.B: Palpation of peripheral pulses in the upper extremities
options.C: Auscultation of bowel sounds and abdominal girth measurement
options.D: Daily checking of deep tendon reflexes in the legs

explanation: Keep an eye on their eyes! Regular vision and color checks catch Ethambutol's eye-related side effects early before they cause permanent harm. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h7)

question: A clinic has funds to build either a new youth center or a borehole for clean water. A community diagnosis shows high rates of waterborne diseases. What should be funded first?

options.A: Both projects equally, regardless of the community health data
options.B: The youth center, because young people complain the loudest
options.C: Neither project, until the national government gives more money
options.D: The borehole, because it addresses the identified health crisis

explanation: Resources must be directed toward solving the specific health threats uncovered during the diagnostic assessment. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which serious medical condition is a very common trigger for acute DIC?

options.A: Essential hypertension
options.B: Chronic osteoarthritis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Severe sepsis

explanation: Severe infections and sepsis release a flood of inflammatory chemicals that accidentally trigger widespread clotting all over the body. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h3)

question: How is disinfection different from sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization takes less time than standard chemical disinfection
options.B: Disinfection is only performed on human skin and living tissues
options.C: Disinfection does not destroy all bacterial spores like sterilization does
options.D: Sterilization uses chemical agents while disinfection only uses heat

explanation: Spot on! Sterilization is the heavy-duty process that wipes out every single trace of life, including tough spores. Disinfection cleans up most germs, but leaves spores behind. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: What surgical instrument is typically used during a standard laparoscopy for tubal ligation?

options.A: A lighted camera scope and small grasping tools
options.B: A large open abdominal retractor and surgical saw
options.C: A long uterine curette inserted through the vagina
options.D: An ultrasound probe placed directly on the ovaries

explanation: Laparoscopy relies on a small camera inserted via a tiny umbilical incision to guide specialized instruments that seal or block the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: A patient on a breathing machine (ventilator) is at high risk for which mouth problem?

options.A: Losing their sense of smell completely and forever
options.B: Sudden growth of wisdom teeth right at the back
options.C: Drooling because of too much natural saliva production
options.D: Fast plaque buildup and ventilator-associated pneumonia

explanation: You've got this! Because intubated patients cannot clean their own teeth and often have dry mouths, germs gather quickly and can travel down to cause pneumonia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: A nurse finishes dressing a wound soaked with infected pus. Where should the soiled gauze dressing be discarded?

options.A: Cardboard medication box
options.B: General recycling container
options.C: Yellow infectious waste bag
options.D: Black domestic waste bin

explanation: Infectious clinical waste containing body fluids goes into the yellow bag to prevent the spread of pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: A hospital pharmacy prices an antibiotic by adding up the supplier price, shipping fees, storage power, and dispensing salaries. What costing approach is this?

options.A: Subsidized emergency pricing
options.B: Full operational cost recovery
options.C: Manufacturer retail pricing
options.D: Direct cost only approach

explanation: Spot on! Including both the price of the drug and all overhead expenses ensures the fund gets back every kobo spent to deliver care. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h3)

question: Where does developing true cultural competence in nursing actually begin?

options.A: Reading advanced textbooks on international medical laws
options.B: Memorizing every religious holiday observed in the country
options.C: Traveling to foreign countries to study local hospital systems
options.D: Recognizing one's own personal biases and cultural assumptions

explanation: Spot on! Self-awareness is key. You first have to understand your own background and biases so they don't mess with the care you give others. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses care about picking a good, solid study design?

options.A: It guarantees that funding will be approved by the hospital board
options.B: It allows the researcher to skip the ethical review process entirely
options.C: It ensures the resulting evidence is strong enough to guide safe patient care
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical analysis in the project

explanation: Spot on! We want to base our bedside nursing on facts we can truly trust to keep our patients safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h1)

question: A hospital unit arranges all high-alert drugs in the exact same alphabetical order in every medication room. What safety design principle is this?

options.A: Complex redundancy
options.B: Punitive discipline
options.C: Manual override
options.D: Standardization

explanation: Exactly! Keeping supplies and medications laid out identically across multiple units prevents confusion and helps nurses find what they need quickly and safely. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h4)

question: A student proposes to study 'every health issue affecting every patient in the country.' What is the main problem with this topic?

options.A: The methodology uses too many statistical tests
options.B: It focuses too much on ethical patient consent
options.C: It relies entirely on recent nursing journals
options.D: The scope is far too broad to be manageable

explanation: A good proposal needs a narrow, focused topic so you can actually finish it successfully without getting overwhelmed! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why is it important to document what the lesion or discharge looks like after swabbing?

options.A: To provide a clear baseline for tracking clinical progress
options.B: To prove to the laboratory technician that a swab was necessary
options.C: To satisfy insurance requirements for billing the laboratory test
options.D: To ensure the patient remembers how the symptoms appeared

explanation: Writing a clear description gives the healthcare team a baseline so they can easily check if the treatment is working during the next visit. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk for a patient who is a 'poor metabolizer' of a drug?

options.A: Rapid elimination of the drug before it can work
options.B: Dangerous buildup and toxicity from standard drug doses
options.C: Immediate destruction of the medication in the stomach
options.D: Total immunity to all forms of oral antibiotics

explanation: Well done! Poor metabolizers break down medicines very slowly, meaning a normal dose can pile up in their system and reach toxic levels. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h2)

question: A digital monitor shows a very high blood pressure for a calm patient who feels totally fine. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Write down the machine's number and walk away to another room
options.B: Check the reading manually using a stethoscope and manual cuff
options.C: Rush to give the patient strong blood pressure-lowering drugs
options.D: Throw the electronic device away and never use it again

explanation: Machines can glitch! If a result doesn't match how the patient looks or feels, always double-check it manually before panicking or treating. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do midwives and nurses carefully check the maternal side of a delivered placenta?

options.A: To locate the insertion site of the amniotic membrane
options.B: To measure the exact length of the umbilical cord
options.C: To check for missing cotyledons that could cause bleeding
options.D: To confirm the baby's exact gestational age at birth

explanation: Those little lobes (cotyledons) must all be accounted for! If even a small piece stays behind in the uterus, it can cause severe postpartum hemorrhage. Always check your placenta! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h1)

question: What is the main chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) released at parasympathetic target organs?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key messenger used by the parasympathetic system to talk to target organs. You're building a strong foundation in pharmacology and physiology! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T31#GNS211_U3_T31_h3)

question: How long does a seizure need to last to be called 'status epilepticus'?

options.A: Longer than five minutes
options.B: At least one full hour
options.C: More than twenty-four hours
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Any seizure lasting past five minutes—or happening back-to-back without waking up—is an emergency called status epilepticus. Quick thinking is vital here! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h8)

question: What is a frequent complication when anxiety is left unmanaged for years?

options.A: Loss of the ability to speak permanently
options.B: Development of clinical depression or substance abuse
options.C: Permanent physical paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Complete immunity to all future infections

explanation: Carrying heavy anxiety day after day takes a massive toll, often leading folks to slip into depression or lean on substances just to cope. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h8)

question: What is the primary emergency goal when nursing a patient with severe antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Discharge the patient home if bleeding stops for ten minutes
options.B: Perform immediate blood chemistry panels before starting IV lines
options.C: Resuscitate the mother and maintain hemodynamic stability
options.D: Immediately induce vaginal delivery using oxytocin infusion

explanation: Saving the mother's life through rapid resuscitation and stabilizing her circulation is always the immediate priority in heavy obstetric bleeding. You are doing wonderfully! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h6)

question: What is the main difference between acute and chronic pain?

options.A: Acute pain is tied to recent tissue injury and resolves with healing, while chronic pain lasts long past the normal healing period.
options.B: Acute pain can be measured with scales, but chronic pain cannot be measured.
options.C: Acute pain requires no medical treatment, whereas chronic pain requires surgery.
options.D: Acute pain only affects internal organs, while chronic pain only affects the skin and muscles.

explanation: Think of acute pain as a sudden alarm bell that stops when healing happens, while chronic pain sticks around long after the injury has healed. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h2)

question: A patient is reading a food label and asks which line is most important for managing their diabetes. What should the nurse point out?

options.A: Total carbohydrates
options.B: Total sodium
options.C: Total calories
options.D: Total protein

explanation: Total carbohydrates have the biggest impact on blood glucose, making it the most critical number on the label for diabetes management. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community needs assessment?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with western doctors
options.B: To identify specific health burdens, preferences, and resource gaps
options.C: To determine which hospitals receive the most funding
options.D: To punish communities that ignore public health warnings

explanation: Spot on! Before starting any health program, a needs assessment helps nurses figure out what local challenges and resources look like on the ground. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why is an ECG called a non-invasive test?

options.A: It is performed entirely on the skin without surgical cuts or entering the body
options.B: It uses radioactive dyes injected directly into the coronary arteries
options.C: It requires general anesthesia to keep the patient calm during the procedure
options.D: It involves placing a small camera inside the chambers of the heart

explanation: Because the stickers go right on the skin with no cuts or needles inside the body, it's totally non-invasive! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T16#GNS213_U1_T16_h1)

question: When a patient experiences a permanent sensory loss, what emotional and psychological response do nurses frequently need to help them manage?

options.A: Grief, social withdrawal, and depression
options.B: Severe memory loss and confusion about time
options.C: Aggression and physical violence toward staff
options.D: Euphoria and unrealistic optimism about recovery

explanation: Losing sight or hearing is a massive life change. Patients often go through a grieving process and might pull away from others, so our empathetic nursing support is crucial here. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h4)

question: A junior nurse sees a mother bleeding heavily after birth but stays quiet because she is scared of the senior doctor. What kind of barrier is this?

options.A: Hierarchical barrier
options.B: Equipment failure
options.C: Alert fatigue
options.D: Confirmation bias

explanation: Spot on. Strict hospital ranks can make junior staff too intimidated to speak up. Patient safety means every voice matters, no matter your rank! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which type of sexually transmitted infection can usually be cured with antibiotics?

options.A: Parasitic infections
options.B: Viral infections
options.C: Bacterial infections
options.D: Fungal infections

explanation: Bacterial STIs, like gonorrhea and chlamydia, can be knocked out easily with the right course of antibiotics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h5)

question: Why is testicular torsion treated as an absolute medical emergency?

options.A: It causes irreversible damage to the prostate gland
options.B: Loss of blood supply can lead to tissue death within hours
options.C: It always leads to permanent systemic high blood pressure
options.D: It immediately spreads severe infection to the kidneys

explanation: You nailed it. When the cord twists, it cuts off blood flow. If we don't fix it right away, the testicle can die. Every minute counts! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h4)

question: When documenting injuries resulting from suspected gender-based violence in the patient's medical record, what is the best practice for a nurse to follow?

options.A: Omit any mention of violence to protect the privacy of the family
options.B: Write down personal opinions about who started the argument in the home
options.C: Describe the injuries vaguely to avoid getting involved in police investigations
options.D: Record exact quotes from the patient and use objective descriptions of physical findings

explanation: Accurate, objective documentation using direct quotes and precise physical descriptions is crucial for both clinical continuity and potential legal proceedings. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h7)

question: What type of care approach is most effective when treating survivors of forced marriage?

options.A: Experimental surgical care
options.B: Strictly punitive care
options.C: Cosmetic dermatological care
options.D: Trauma-informed care

explanation: Trauma-informed care acknowledges the profound psychological impact of abuse and focuses on safety, trust, and empowerment for the survivor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h7)

question: How do in-text citations connect to your reference list at the end?

options.A: The reference list contains sources you read but did not cite
options.B: They use completely different formatting styles from each other
options.C: Every in-text citation must match a full entry in the reference list
options.D: In-text citations are only used if the reference list is missing

explanation: Think of them as best friends: if you mention a source in your paragraph, it must have its full home address in your reference list! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which factor can cause a pulse oximeter sensor to give an inaccurate reading on a patient's finger?

options.A: Cold fingers and poor peripheral circulation
options.B: Speaking in a normal tone of voice during the test
options.C: Drinking a glass of cold water before testing
options.D: A high room temperature on the hospital ward

explanation: Pulse oximeters rely on good blood flow through the finger; if circulation is sluggish or cold, the machine cannot read the pulse well. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the biggest perk of doing a quick mental check-in with yourself at the end of a shift?

options.A: Eliminating the requirement for formal nursing handover reports
options.B: Ensuring that the morning shift arrives earlier than scheduled
options.C: Identifying workflow delays to improve future time management
options.D: Calculating the exact financial savings generated for the hospital

explanation: You're learning fast! Thinking about what slowed you down today helps you plan better and feel more confident tomorrow. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h7)

question: How does research directly help you practice evidence-based care on the ward?

options.A: It dictates the exact salary scale for nursing staff
options.B: It eliminates all documentation requirements for nurses
options.C: It replaces the need to assess individual patient preferences
options.D: It provides tested proof of which clinical interventions work best

explanation: Correct! Research gives us the reliable facts we need to update our daily ward procedures and get better results for our patients. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a common reason why conflicts start in a hospital ward?

options.A: Ambiguous roles and unclear scopes of practice
options.B: Too many open nursing positions on the ward
options.C: An excess of available medical equipment
options.D: Identical personalities among all staff members

explanation: When people aren't quite sure where their duties end and someone else's begin, misunderstandings and friction are bound to happen. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h2)

question: If an air ring is specially ordered for a patient, what is the correct way to prepare it?

options.A: Place it directly against bare skin without any cover
options.B: Inflate it to maximum capacity for firm support
options.C: Fill it with warm water instead of air
options.D: Inflate it only slightly and cover it with a soft sheet

explanation: Spot on! Inflating it just a little bit keeps hard edges from digging into the skin, and a clean cover adds an extra layer of comfort. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h4)

question: A community nurse is advising Nigerian mothers on affordable toddler meals. Which approach works best?

options.A: Tell mothers to avoid local vegetables because they lack minerals
options.B: Encourage combining local staples like beans and grains to make balanced meals
options.C: Insist that only imported tinned foods provide enough vitamins for growth
options.D: Advise mothers to feed the child only once a day with a large heavy meal

explanation: Brilliant! Using affordable local foods like beans and maize is sustainable, cost-effective, and keeps our little ones well-nourished. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h7)

question: A patient is healing from a major surgery and needs help repairing skin and tissues. Which nutrient should you encourage?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Saturated fats
options.C: Simple starches
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Well done! Surgical wounds need plenty of protein to rebuild skin, muscle, and internal structures back to health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h2)

question: What does host susceptibility mean in the context of infectious disease?

options.A: A lack of resistance making the host vulnerable to an infection
options.B: The rate at which a pathogen multiplies inside blood vessels
options.C: The ability of an organism to completely destroy all local bacteria
options.D: A genetic immunity passed down through multiple family generations

explanation: Susceptibility is simply the vulnerability or lack of immunity an individual has against a specific infectious agent. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h3)

question: A patient's chest tube accidentally falls completely out of their chest. What should you do immediately?

options.A: Leave the open chest wound completely uncovered and run to find a doctor
options.B: Put clean gloves on and push the exact same tube back into the chest wound
options.C: Clamp the remaining chest tubing tightly to preserve negative pressure
options.D: Cover the site with a sterile petroleum dressing taped on three sides

explanation: A three-sided petroleum dressing acts like a smart flap—it lets trapped air escape while stopping room air from sucking back in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for the vomiting reflex?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Cerebral cortex
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: Great job! The vomiting center sits right in the medulla oblongata of the brainstem, pulling together different nerve signals to trigger vomiting. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is delayed bathing recommended for stable newborns immediately after birth?

options.A: It allows the umbilical cord stump to dry
options.B: It helps preserve vernix for skin immunity
options.C: It prevents early neonatal jaundice spikes
options.D: It prevents rapid heat loss and cold stress

explanation: Washing a wet baby too soon strips away heat through evaporation, putting them at high risk for dangerous drops in body temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h4)

question: Why can steroid hormones slip right out of cells as soon as they are made?

options.A: They are pushed out by water pressure inside the cytoplasm
options.B: They are small enough to pass through active transport protein pumps
options.C: They are stored in large vesicles that burst open upon stimulation
options.D: They are fat-soluble and can cross lipid cell membranes easily

explanation: Because cell membranes are also made of fats (lipids), fat-loving steroid hormones pass straight through them like an open door—no special channels needed! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h4)

question: How can strict, old-fashioned gender roles negatively affect relationships?

options.A: They encourage equal sharing of household responsibilities
options.B: They can promote power imbalances and discourage emotional expression
options.C: They ensure that partners always agree on financial decisions
options.D: They eliminate all forms of misunderstandings between couples

explanation: Exactly! When society forces rigid boxes on how men and women must behave, it often stops open communication and creates unfair power dynamics. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h7)

question: What is the main goal of sperm capacitation inside the female reproductive tract?

options.A: To prepare the sperm membrane and make it capable of fertilizing the oocyte
options.B: To slow down sperm movement so they rest before reaching the egg
options.C: To increase the total volume of seminal fluid for easier transport
options.D: To attach extra chromosomes to the sperm tail for genetic diversity

explanation: Capacitation is like a final readiness training. It changes the sperm's membrane so it gains the strength to pierce the egg's outer layers. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h3)

question: When did the World Health Organization (WHO) publish its first Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: Great try! The WHO put out this very first list back in 1977 to bring order, safety, and priority to global drug markets. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when trying to prevent adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Guessing the patient's weight without asking them
options.B: Checking the patient's allergy history before giving drugs
options.C: Asking about local herbs and supplements
options.D: Following the five rights of medication administration

explanation: Never guess! Drug doses must be exact, especially for vulnerable patients. Always measure or ask for accurate weights. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h6)

question: A patient comes to the clinic asking about her risk for an ectopic pregnancy. Which factor in her history raises her risk the most?

options.A: Eating a diet low in green leafy vegetables and iron
options.B: A previous ectopic pregnancy in her medical history
options.C: A family history of high blood pressure during labor
options.D: Having a normal, healthy full-term delivery last year

explanation: Having had a past ectopic pregnancy is one of the strongest risk factors for experiencing another one in the future. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h3)

question: Why do you need to watch the needle site extra carefully after drawing blood from someone with severe liver disease?

options.A: Their veins are usually completely collapsed from chronic fluid overload
options.B: Their skin is too fragile to tolerate standard adhesive tape
options.C: They often have poor clotting due to low production of clotting factors
options.D: Local anesthetics used during the draw can cause severe allergic reactions

explanation: You nailed it! A struggling liver can't pump out enough clotting proteins, meaning your patient is at a higher risk of prolonged bleeding or bruising after a needle stick. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h5)

question: How do healthy endothelial cells help prevent abnormal blood clotting?

options.A: By triggering the intrinsic pathway during normal circulation
options.B: By releasing substances that actively inhibit platelet sticking
options.C: By producing large amounts of active thrombin into the blood
options.D: By slowing down the heart rate to reduce blood turbulence

explanation: Intact endothelium produces chemicals like prostacyclin and nitric oxide that discourage platelets from clumping together on normal vessel walls. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why does leftover tissue inside the uterus sharply increase the risk of infection?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature below normal levels.
options.B: It stops the liver from producing infection-fighting proteins.
options.C: It provides an ideal environment for bacteria to multiply.
options.D: It directly inactivates all circulating white blood cells.

explanation: Bacteria love stagnant, dead tissue mixed with blood! Leftover tissue creates a cozy breeding ground where bacteria can easily multiply and cause infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h4)

question: What is the main danger when handling genotoxic healthcare waste, such as cancer chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: Sudden acute bacterial infections
options.B: Severe electrolyte imbalance
options.C: Damage to cellular DNA and cancer risk
options.D: Immediate thermal skin burns

explanation: Genotoxic means 'toxic to genes.' These powerful drugs mess with cell DNA, which can cause mutations or cancer over time if we don't handle them with strict care. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h3)

question: What do we call a nurse's ability to understand and respect a patient's cultural beliefs while giving great care?

options.A: Cultural competence
options.B: Clinical detachment
options.C: Legal negligence
options.D: Medical paternalism

explanation: Cultural competence helps you bridge cultural and religious gaps so you can care for your patients safely and respectfully. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is the secret behind why Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) works so well?

options.A: Water absorption is stimulated by adding high amounts of sugar
options.B: Sodium and glucose transport together, pulling water into the body
options.C: Glucose completely paralyzes the nerves that cause bowel spasms
options.D: Sodium creates a thick barrier that blocks toxins from entering

explanation: Sodium and glucose team up in the gut wall. Even when you have diarrhoea, this special transport team helps pull water right back into your body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h6)

question: What does a susceptible host represent in the chain of infection?

options.A: A medical instrument sterilized prior to a procedure
options.B: A person who lacks resistance to a specific pathogen
options.C: The physical surface where bacteria live and multiply
options.D: The specific pathway a virus uses to leave the body

explanation: A susceptible host is an individual whose immune system is weak or compromised enough to allow an infection to take hold. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)?

options.A: To show the minimum amount of food needed to avoid fatigue
options.B: To determine the cheapest food sources of essential vitamins
options.C: To warn against taking dangerously high amounts of a nutrient
options.D: To calculate the exact number of calories burned during rest

explanation: Think of the UL as a safety warning light. It tells us the highest amount of a nutrient a person can take before it starts causing harm, especially from supplements. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h2)

question: In clinic practice, what do we call a family planning client who misses their scheduled visit or refill date?

options.A: A client who misses a scheduled clinic visit or contraceptive refill
options.B: A woman who refuses to discuss contraception with a nurse
options.C: A client who chooses to switch contraceptive methods
options.D: A patient who permanently stops all healthcare interactions

explanation: A defaulter is simply someone who misses their expected return date for supplies or check-ins. Spotting this early lets us reach out and support them! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h1)

question: Why do patients sometimes feel tummy pain during the early stage of this infection?

options.A: Adult worms multiply inside the lower digestive tract
options.B: Toxins from the lung flukes specifically target the stomach lining
options.C: Juvenile worms burrow through the intestinal wall and belly lining
options.D: Bad bacteria grow from eating contaminated food

explanation: You got it! Once the baby flukes hatch in the gut, they have to crawl right through the gut wall and up toward the lungs, causing some local irritation along the way. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h4)

question: Which skill became essential for nurses as critical care established itself as a distinct specialty?

options.A: Managing hospital financial budgets and payroll for nursing units
options.B: Performing major abdominal surgeries independently in an emergency
options.C: Interpreting complex hemodynamic parameters and monitor waveforms
options.D: Conducting long-term outpatient psychiatric counseling sessions

explanation: Specialized nurses learned to read intricate data from monitors to catch subtle signs of patient deterioration early. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why must nurses be extra careful when giving psychiatric drugs to patients with brain degeneration?

options.A: These drugs completely stop the physical progression of the genetic disease
options.B: Medications only work if they are given through an intravenous line
options.C: Their damaged brains make them more sensitive to side effects like excessive sedation
options.D: Patients with degenerative conditions are immune to all forms of chemical treatment

explanation: Brilliant. Because the central nervous system is altered, even small doses can cause strong side effects like heavy sleepiness. Always start low and go slow! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: What is the route of transmission?

options.A: The time it takes for a disease to show its first symptoms
options.B: The specific path a pathogen takes from its source to a new host
options.C: The total number of microbes required to cause an infection
options.D: The chemical makeup of an infectious agent's outer shell

explanation: The route of transmission is simply the way a germ travels from where it lives to a person who can catch it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: A patient presents with severe breast tissue necrosis and chronic infections following breast ironing. What is the primary reason for these complications?

options.A: A genetic predisposition to skin weakness
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard cotton clothing
options.C: Lack of proper vitamins in the daily diet
options.D: Repeated thermal burns and deep tissue crushing

explanation: Applying intense heat and heavy pressure directly breaks down skin and underlying flesh, causing wounds and dead tissue. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h4)

question: A patient receives several bags of packed red blood cells after an accident, but no plasma. What clotting complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Vitamin K toxicity
options.B: Dilutive coagulopathy
options.C: Hereditary hemophilia A
options.D: Polycythemia vera

explanation: If you only pump in red blood cells without replacing plasma, you end up diluting the patient's remaining platelets and clotting factors. This is called dilutive coagulopathy. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of medical asepsis?

options.A: To reduce the number of germs and stop them from spreading
options.B: To remove every single microorganism and bacterial spore
options.C: To create a pathogen-free environment inside the body cavity
options.D: To sterilize surgical instruments before an operation

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on decreasing the overall load of microorganisms to prevent cross-contamination during routine care. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why do market porters who carry heavy loads on their heads often suffer from chronic back and neck pain?

options.A: They suffer from acute biological infections spread by insects
options.B: They experience psychosocial stress from working long hours
options.C: They are exposed to dangerous chemical solvents in the market
options.D: They face severe ergonomic strain from heavy lifting and poor posture

explanation: Balancing heavy loads incorrectly puts immense pressure on the spine and supporting muscles, leading to long-term pain. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h4)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) so important specifically in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Hospital management requires it only for decorative uniformity
options.B: It prevents dust from settling on the clean instruments
options.C: The temperature in that specific room is extremely high
options.D: Staff are exposed to blood splashes, contaminated water, and sharp tools

explanation: Spot on! Because you are washing blood-stained, used instruments, PPE acts as your shield against splashes, dirty water, and accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: A teenage client is super shy and hesitant to talk about sexual health. What should you do first as their nurse?

options.A: Create a safe, confidential, and non-judgmental environment
options.B: Call the client's parents into the room immediately
options.C: Skip the sexual health assessment entirely
options.D: Scold the client for being immature about health matters

explanation: Brilliant nursing instinct! Trust and a warm, welcoming vibe help nervous clients relax and open up to care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)

question: Which finding is considered a vital part of assessing a patient with a suspected emerging infection?

options.A: Evaluating the patient's current employment income level
options.B: Checking the patient's past childhood immunization cards
options.C: Measuring the patient's daily fluid intake at home
options.D: A detailed travel and recent exposure history

explanation: Knowing where a patient has traveled and who they have been in contact with is essential for identifying rare or outbreak-related pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: A nurse manager sees that patient falls are increasing on the ward. What should they do first?

options.A: Suspend all nursing staff on duty immediately
options.B: Review incident reports and audit unit safety practices
options.C: Ignore the data because falls are common in hospitals
options.D: Give every patient a written academic test on mobility

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions, always look at the data and evaluate the root cause so you can fix the actual problem. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h7)

question: Which global health body leads the way in setting standards for medical waste management?

options.A: International Monetary Fund
options.B: World Health Organization
options.C: International Labour Organization
options.D: World Trade Organization

explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides the main guidelines and handbooks that countries follow to keep medical waste disposal safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: Why do lymph nodes often swell up and feel tender when you have an infection?

options.A: White blood cells multiply rapidly inside the node to fight pathogens
options.B: Blood flow to the node temporarily stops completely
options.C: Trapped fluid stretches the outer capsule of the node permanently
options.D: Red blood cells leak out of nearby capillaries into the node

explanation: When germs arrive, your white blood cells throw a massive defense party inside the node, multiplying quickly to fight off the infection. That crowding is what causes the swelling and tenderness! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why is Family Life Education an important part of primary health care?

options.A: It eliminates all infectious diseases from the community
options.B: It guarantees financial stability for every household
options.C: It completely replaces the need for hospital-based doctors
options.D: It equips individuals with knowledge to make healthy life choices

explanation: When people get the right information about their bodies and relationships, they can make smart choices to protect their health! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h1)

question: How does dietary counselling differ from Medical Nutrition Therapy?

options.A: There is no real difference between the two terms in clinical practice
options.B: Counselling is only done by surgeons in the operating theatre
options.C: MNT is used exclusively for people who want to lose weight for fashion
options.D: Counselling focuses on general healthy eating, whereas MNT treats complex disease states

explanation: Dietary counselling covers general wellness and basic lifestyle tips, while MNT is an intensive clinical treatment for specific diseases. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: What is a common social and physical complication of an untreated vaginal fistula?

options.A: Complete overgrowth of protective lactobacilli
options.B: Rapid thickening of the vaginal epithelial walls
options.C: Sudden onset of primary amenorrhea in teenagers
options.D: Continuous leakage leading to skin breakdown and isolation

explanation: Fistulas cause constant involuntary leakage of urine or stool, resulting in severe hygiene challenges, skin irritation, and social distress. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why should you warn patients taking regular NSAIDs to steer clear of alcohol?

options.A: It lowers blood sugar to dangerous emergency levels
options.B: It causes immediate and permanent kidney destruction
options.C: It drastically increases the risk of stomach bleeding and ulcers
options.D: It completely stops the pain-relieving action of the drug

explanation: Alcohol and NSAIDs are a harsh double-whammy for the gastric lining. Mixing them together invites nasty stomach irritation and bleeding. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h7)

question: A critically ill patient just received a lot of IV fluids. Which sign helps you catch early fluid overload?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on both lower legs
options.B: A slight drop in body temperature
options.C: Developing crackles in the lung bases
options.D: An increase in the patient's daily appetite

explanation: Too much fluid in the system quickly backs up into the lungs, creating those classic crackling sounds when you listen with your stethoscope. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h7)

question: The surgeon is about to close the patient's tummy. What specific count must happen right now?

options.A: The midnight stock inventory
options.B: The post-operative ward count
options.C: The preoperative equipment check
options.D: The cavity closure count

explanation: Before closing up deep spaces, a closure count is mandatory to double-check that no materials are trapped inside. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: When a hospital is planning space for future needs, what data is most important to look at?

options.A: The architectural styles used in other commercial buildings
options.B: Patient admission trends and local population changes
options.C: The cost of office furniture and administrative supplies
options.D: The personal preferences of the hospital board members

explanation: To plan for tomorrow, planners must check how many patients have been coming in and how the local community is growing. It is all about meeting real community needs! [learn more](GST321_U4_T5#GST321_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the main limitation of relying solely on national laws to stop harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Courts are legally forbidden from hearing domestic abuse cases
options.B: Laws cannot change deep social beliefs without community engagement
options.C: Law enforcement officers are exempt from handling family matters
options.D: International treaties always override local criminal statutes

explanation: Legislation provides penalties, but if the community still values the tradition, practices simply go underground. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard piece of guidance a nurse should give to promote healthy circulation in a pregnant woman?

options.A: Avoid standing motionless in one spot for long periods of time
options.B: Change positions slowly when getting up from a chair or bed
options.C: Sleep on your side to prevent compression of major blood vessels
options.D: Lie completely flat on your back whenever resting during the day

explanation: Lying flat on the back compresses the vena cava and drops cardiac output, so side-lying positions are strongly preferred. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: Which of these is a normal breathing change in older adults?

options.A: Enhanced vital capacity
options.B: Increased lung elastic recoil
options.C: Reduced chest wall compliance
options.D: Rapid expansion of alveoli

explanation: As we age, the cartilage in our chest wall gets a bit stiff (reduced compliance), making it slightly harder for the chest to expand as easily as it used to. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the medical term for dangerously high blood sugar?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Hypokalemia
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Hyperglycemia just means too much glucose floating in the blood. You've got this! Keep building that nursing vocabulary. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h1)

question: A client wants to use the rhythm method, but her husband refuses to help or participate in cycle tracking. What should you do?

options.A: Refuse to provide any further healthcare services at the clinic
options.B: Tell her to force her husband to read the calendar against his will
options.C: Sign her up for the rhythm method anyway without mentioning her husband
options.D: Counsel the client on the need for partner cooperation and discuss alternative methods she can control independently

explanation: Methods like rhythm and withdrawal take teamwork. If her partner isn't on board, guide her toward choices she can manage completely on her own, like injectables or implants. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h8)

question: How do free radicals and reactive oxygen species primarily damage our cells?

options.A: By stimulating excessive and uncontrollable cellular reproduction
options.B: By instantly freezing intracellular fluid and stopping circulation
options.C: By creating oxidative stress that harms DNA and cell membranes
options.D: By completely blocking the intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Free radicals love to steal electrons from nearby molecules. This creates oxidative stress, which can rough up essential parts of the cell like our DNA and protective membranes. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h4)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is the embryo most sensitive to harmful substances (teratogens) that cause birth defects?

options.A: During gametogenesis before fertilization
options.B: The first week prior to implantation
options.C: The final trimester before birth
options.D: Weeks three through eight during organogenesis

explanation: Correct! Weeks 3 to 8 are when all the major organs are actively forming, making this a critical window where they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h7)

question: What key detail does a drug label tell you about its strength?

options.A: The amount of active drug per tablet, capsule, or milliliter
options.B: The name of the drug rep
options.C: The patient's diagnosis
options.D: How much the hospital paid for it

explanation: The label strength tells you the concentration—how much medicine is actually packed into each pill or mL. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h5)

question: Why are progestin-only pills usually recommended for breastfeeding mothers instead of combined oral pills?

options.A: They provide permanent protection after a single dose
options.B: They do not interfere with breast milk production
options.C: They completely stop all menstrual bleeding forever
options.D: They protect the mother against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Since progestin-only pills don't have estrogen, they keep a mother's milk supply safe and flowing for her baby. Brilliant clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h3)

question: What role do abnormal proteins play in degenerative neurological disorders?

options.A: They protect neurons from oxidative stress
options.B: They form harmful clumps that disrupt cell function
options.C: They speed up normal electrical signals
options.D: They help repair damaged nerve pathways

explanation: Proteins that fold incorrectly build up inside or around nerve cells, interfering with normal operations and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which leadership style works best with the core philosophy of team nursing?

options.A: Democratic leadership involving mutual respect
options.B: Strict autocratic control by auxiliary staff
options.C: Total absence of leadership or direction
options.D: Remote management from outside the hospital

explanation: Well done! Team nursing thrives when the leader respects every member and encourages collaboration instead of just barking harsh commands. Great ward dynamics! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical sign of an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Fever and severe lower back pain
options.B: Sudden drop in body temperature and shivering
options.C: Chest tightness and feeling of impending doom
options.D: Dark-colored urine caused by free hemoglobin

explanation: Watch out for trick questions like this! Transfusion reactions usually cause a fever, not a drop in temperature, along with back pain, dark urine, and anxiety. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h6)

question: How can the government best tackle the problem of nurses refusing postings to remote rural clinics due to poor living conditions?

options.A: Closing down all rural clinics and building more hospitals in the capital city
options.B: Firing all nurses who refuse urban postings without investigation
options.C: Removing nurses entirely from the primary healthcare system
