options.D: Offering rural hardship allowances and improved housing for health workers

explanation: Providing financial incentives and safe housing makes it much easier and fairer for health workers to serve in remote areas. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why do many patients find it hard to stick to a low-sodium diet at first?

options.A: Fresh vegetables completely lose all their nutritional value
options.B: Taste buds take time to adjust, making food taste bland initially
options.C: The human brain loses the ability to feel thirsty
options.D: Low-sodium foods are chemically impossible for the stomach to digest

explanation: Exactly! Our taste buds need a little patience to readjust to less salt, but once they do, natural food flavors start shining through! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h6)

question: What is the best test to confirm the exact bilirubin level in a newborn?

options.A: Transcutaneous skin scanner
options.B: Serum bilirubin blood test
options.C: Urine color comparison chart
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: While skin scanners are quick, a blood test gives the exact measurement the doctor needs to decide if phototherapy is necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: Why does the actual amount of oxygen (FiO2) a patient receives from a nasal cannula vary from person to person?

options.A: Different hospitals calibrate their wall oxygen outlets to different pressures
options.B: It depends on the patient's breathing rate and depth, which mixes room air with the oxygen
options.C: Patients absorb oxygen at different speeds through their skin
options.D: The plastic tubing stretches or shrinks based on the room temperature

explanation: Because a nasal cannula is an open system, patients breathe in regular room air right along with the oxygen. How fast or deep they breathe changes the exact mix! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h5)

question: The doctor orders 500 mg of a syrup, and your stock bottle reads 250 mg per 5 mL. How many milliliters will you give?

options.A: 20 mL
options.B: 5 mL
options.C: 2.5 mL
options.D: 10 mL

explanation: Let's use the simple formula: (Desired ÷ Stock) × Volume. That's (500 ÷ 250) × 5 = 2 × 5 = 10 mL. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of home health care nursing?

options.A: To help patients manage health conditions in their own living space
options.B: To replace family members in making all daily household decisions
options.C: To isolate patients from infectious community environments
options.D: To provide permanent round-the-clock intensive care for all clients

explanation: Spot on! Home health nursing is all about bringing professional care right to where the patient lives, helping them recover and manage chronic conditions comfortably. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main goal of building a safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Ensuring hospitals meet strict financial profit margins
options.B: Reducing the total number of employed nursing personnel
options.C: Prioritizing patient protection from accidental harm above all else
options.D: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors

explanation: Spot on! A safety culture is all about putting patient safety first and making sure everyone works together to prevent accidental harm. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: Distributing medical supplies to rural clinics
options.B: Diagnosing rare tropical infectious diseases
options.C: Writing detailed hospital administration reports
options.D: Promoting positive and sustainable health habits

explanation: You've got this! BCC is all about using interactive ways to help people and communities build healthy habits that actually last. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h1)

question: Why is taking a nighttime dose of a cystine-binding medication so important?

options.A: Cystine excretion often peaks at night during periods of sleep and dehydration
options.B: Kidney blood flow drops to zero during deep sleep, requiring higher drug levels
options.C: Bedtime dosing completely eliminates the need for daytime water intake
options.D: The liver metabolizes the medication much faster during daylight hours

explanation: At night, we sleep without drinking water, making our urine concentrated. A bedtime dose protects the kidneys during those vulnerable overnight hours! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h4)

question: What is the main focus of primary prevention programs for substance abuse in communities?

options.A: Providing emergency medical care for patients suffering from drug overdose
options.B: Educating youth about the dangers of drugs and how to resist peer pressure
options.C: Punishing individuals who sell illegal substances on the street
options.D: Managing acute withdrawal symptoms inside a hospital detox unit

explanation: You got it! Primary prevention stops the problem before it even starts by giving young people the right information and strong coping tools early on. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h8)

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h3)

question: Why is knowing when ovulation happens so important for natural family planning?

options.A: It stops the ovaries from producing estrogen during the rest of the month
options.B: It guarantees that menstruation will arrive on the exact same day every month
options.C: It marks the exact days when unprotected intercourse can lead to pregnancy
options.D: It shortens the total length of the menstrual cycle over time

explanation: Spotting ovulation helps couples know the exact fertile window. Since the released egg lives only a short time, this timing is key for planning or avoiding pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing duty when caring for patients on medication?

options.A: Changing the chemical composition of the drug in the IV bag
options.B: Evaluating lab results related to drug metabolism and excretion
options.C: Assessing the patient for unexpected adverse drug reactions
options.D: Checking vital signs to verify therapeutic effectiveness

explanation: Nurses administer and monitor, but altering drug formulas is strictly for pharmacists and manufacturers. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h5)

question: As a nurse, you receive new paracetamol expiring in 2026, but the shelf already has stock expiring in 2025. What should you do?

options.A: Place the 2025 stock in front and dispense it before the 2026 stock
options.B: Mix all the tablets together in one big container
options.C: Return both supplies immediately to the central medical store
options.D: Place the 2026 stock in front and keep the 2025 stock behind

explanation: Great clinical habit! Always use the ones expiring sooner (2025) so nothing spoils on the shelf. That's true nursing resourcefulness. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a primary benefit of school feeding programmes?

options.A: Improving student concentration and cognitive development
options.B: Increasing the school fees paid by parents
options.C: Replacing the role of parents in family budgeting
options.D: Eliminating the need for any teaching staff

explanation: Adequate nutrition provides the energy and nutrients required for active learning and brain development. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is an asymptomatic carrier?

options.A: A host who harbors an infectious agent without showing illness but can still spread it
options.B: A patient who has completely recovered and has lifelong immunity to a virus
options.C: An environmental surface that holds bacteria without allowing them to multiply
options.D: An animal that serves as the final dead-end host for a dangerous parasite

explanation: An asymptomatic carrier feels totally fine and shows no signs of sickness, but they are secretly carrying and spreading the germ to others. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h4)

question: Why do our cells constantly need metabolic processes?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluids
options.B: They maintain basic life functions and support tissue repair
options.C: They regulate blood pressure by controlling kidney size
options.D: They prevent all forms of bacterial and viral infections

explanation: Cells are tiny powerhouses! They rely on ongoing metabolism to make energy, heal wounds, and keep your body running smoothly every single day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h1)

question: Why is a clean cloth or gauze used between the skin and the poultice paste?

options.A: To keep the application neat and hold the paste together
options.B: To cure the infection without using any medicine
options.C: To completely block all heat from reaching the patient
options.D: To prevent the nurse from wearing clean gloves

explanation: The cloth acts as a barrier that contains the messy paste while allowing warmth and medicinal properties to pass through. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: If a data point on a control chart suddenly shoots way past the upper limit, what should the nursing team do?

options.A: Investigate for a special cause driving the unusual result
options.B: Assume the charting software has a permanent calculation error
options.C: Ignore it because minor daily fluctuations are totally normal
options.D: Immediately rewrite all hospital policies from the ground up

explanation: You're doing great! When a point falls way outside the normal lines, it's a signal to look closer and find out what unusual thing happened. [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h3)

question: A widow of eight months says daily that she wishes she were dead to join her husband and won't leave her house. What should you do?

options.A: Reassure her that wanting to join her husband is completely normal
options.B: Refer the patient for immediate mental health evaluation and counseling
options.C: Advise her to take up a new hobby to distract her mind from sadness
options.D: Wait another four months before taking any clinical action

explanation: Safety first! Talk of wanting to die combined with severe withdrawal means the patient needs immediate professional mental health support. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the absolute first thing to check and manage when a patient is brought in with a suspected drug overdose?

options.A: Drawing blood for lab tests
options.B: Finding out the exact name of the drug taken
options.C: Administering activated charcoal orally
options.D: Securing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: You've got this! Always remember the ABCs (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) come first in any emergency. We keep the patient alive and breathing before we worry about detective work or giving specific medications. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h1)

question: How does drug absorption in the lower rectum affect metabolism?

options.A: It sends all medications directly to the stomach
options.B: It destroys the active ingredients instantly
options.C: It forces the drug to be stored in the kidneys
options.D: It bypasses the liver's first-pass metabolism

explanation: Lower rectal veins carry the drug straight into the general circulation, skipping the quick breakdown by the liver that oral pills face. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h4)

question: What does the abbreviation 'bid' mean on a medication order?

options.A: As needed
options.B: Before meals
options.C: Twice a day
options.D: Three times a day

explanation: You've got this! 'Bid' comes from the Latin 'bis in die', which simply means twice daily. You'll see this all the time on drug charts! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why are ACE inhibitor medications often given to kidney disease patients even if their blood pressure is completely normal?

options.A: They stimulate the bone marrow to produce extra white blood cells.
options.B: They absorb extra phosphorus directly from the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: They reduce pressure inside the glomeruli and decrease protein leakage.
options.D: They dissolve calcium deposits that form inside the renal tubules.

explanation: Think of ACE inhibitors as pressure-relieving valves for the nephrons. By easing the internal filtering pressure, they protect the kidneys from wearing out faster. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a key part of the birth plan you should discuss with a mother during a home visit?

options.A: Arranging emergency transport and saving money
options.B: Choosing the baby's future university
options.C: Buying expensive imported baby clothes
options.D: Booking a private hotel room for recovery

explanation: Birth preparedness is practical! Having transport sorted and a bit of cash saved can literally save a life when labor starts. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T4#GNS225_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which portable device does a patient wear to continuously send heart rhythm data to the nurse's station?

options.A: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.B: A handheld blood glucose meter
options.C: A telemetry transmitter
options.D: A basic digital thermometer

explanation: Telemetry packs are worn by the patient to wirelessly beam their ECG rhythm straight to the central monitor. Very handy for cardiac patients! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why do we need to make sure we have enough trained staff before starting a health program?

options.A: To guarantee that administrative tasks take precedence over patient care
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement set by international donor agencies
options.C: To ensure the workforce can handle the service volume without burning out
options.D: To prevent the community from ever questioning clinical decisions

explanation: Matching your team size to the expected crowd keeps patients happy and protects our hardworking nurses from burnout. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h2)

question: What is a major economic barrier to healthcare access for many low-income families in Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive abundance of free community health centers
options.B: Strict government bans on traditional herbal medicines
options.C: Out-of-pocket payment for medical services and medications
options.D: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens

explanation: Without broad health insurance, many families have to pay cash directly for consultations, labs, and drugs, which can be tough. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of giving Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT)?

options.A: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes
options.B: To provide daily nutritional caloric requirements

question: Which position usually helps relieve sharp chest pain for a patient with acute pericarditis?

question: A nurse notices a husband is dominating the conversation and suspects his wife is hiding health issues. What is the best first step?

question: Why do different birth control methods have different follow-up timetables?

question: Why do nurses divide the belly into four quarters (quadrants) during physical checks?

question: Which principle ensures that health services are affordable and located where young people can easily reach them?

question: A relative panics after noticing strange, irregular breathing patterns in a dying patient. How do you respond?

question: Why are nurses in a great position to act as health educators?

question: Damage to which part of the brain is primarily responsible for the balance and coordination problems seen in ataxic cerebral palsy?

question: A patient sits crying silently in bed after receiving a terminal diagnosis. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

question: Which part of the digestive tract does Ulcerative Colitis affect?

question: Why is a democratic leadership style poorly suited for a sudden emergency in the emergency department?

question: A patient is scared to take a new blood pressure medicine because their neighbor had a bad rash from it. What is the best nursing response?

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from foods you are ready to eat?

question: Why are hospitals and clinics often the first places to spot survivors of gender-based violence?

question: A patient experiences a sudden drop in heart rate and active digestion after eating a large meal. Which system is most active?

question: What is the recommended minimum time a mother should wait before getting pregnant again, to protect her health and her child's?

question: Why are palliative patients at such high risk for developing pressure injuries?

question: A quality improvement nurse is reviewing patient falls over the past year. How can a histogram help?

question: Why is it so crucial for a community nurse to track and report disease numbers quickly?

options.A: It prevents patients from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It guarantees immediate promotion within the nursing profession
options.C: It allows for early detection and rapid containment of disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the need for community health education programs

explanation: Well done! Catching an unusual spike in illnesses early helps public health teams jump in and stop an outbreak before it goes wild. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h5)

question: How does poverty negatively affect the reproductive health of women in resource-limited settings?

options.A: It legally bars them from entering public health facilities
options.B: It guarantees that they will receive substandard care from international doctors
options.C: It prevents them from paying for transport, diagnostics, and essential medications
options.D: It automatically increases their biological fertility rate beyond normal levels

explanation: Out-of-pocket costs for transport, tests, and drugs are tough barriers that often force struggling women to miss out on the vital care they need. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does cervical cancer usually develop over time?

options.A: It begins slowly as pre-cancerous cellular changes before invading
options.B: It spreads directly from the ovaries within a few days
options.C: It appears suddenly as a widespread systemic blood infection
options.D: It forms from scar tissue after normal childbirth

explanation: Don't worry, it doesn't happen overnight! It starts with quiet, abnormal cell changes that take years to become true cancer. That is why screening is so powerful. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: Which skin receptor is especially good at sensing deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Free nerve ending
options.B: Merkel disc
options.C: Meissner's corpuscle
options.D: Pacinian corpuscle

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are deep in the dermis and act like tiny sensors for strong pressure and vibrations. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h6)

question: What makes a host a 'dead-end host' during an infection?

options.A: The host destroys the infectious agent completely upon first contact
options.B: The host harbors the adult parasite for many years without harm
options.C: The host cannot pass the infection on to other susceptible individuals
options.D: The host dies immediately before any symptoms can manifest

explanation: Think of it as a dead-end street. The pathogen gets stuck inside this host and cannot travel any further to infect other people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h2)

question: If a virus has a strict 14-day incubation period, how long must close contacts be watched?

options.A: Fourteen full days from the last time they were exposed
options.B: Just three days, because most people fall sick fast
options.C: Until a lab test comes back negative
options.D: Only until the first afternoon they feel tired

explanation: Monitoring has to cover the entire possible window to catch late bloomers before they can spread the virus in the community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h5)

question: Which class of diuretics is known for being the most powerful at removing fluid from the body?

options.A: Potassium-sparing diuretics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Thiazide diuretics
options.D: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors

explanation: Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where a massive amount of sodium is normally reabsorbed, making them very potent. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: What does a 'cycloplegic' drug do when dropped into the eye?

options.A: Increases the drainage of fluid from the eye chambers
options.B: Constricts the pupil down to a tiny pinpoint size
options.C: Numbs the surface of the cornea for a quick check
options.D: Paralyzes the focusing muscle inside the eye

explanation: Cycloplegics put the ciliary muscle on pause so it can't focus. This is super helpful during eye exams or surgeries when the eye needs to stay completely relaxed. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: What happens to the pelvic joints to help the baby pass through the birth canal during labor?

options.A: They yield and allow slight widening of the pelvic ring.
options.B: They lock firmly in place to protect the spinal cord.
options.C: They shrink in size to push the baby downward.
options.D: They temporarily fuse into a single solid bone.

explanation: Relaxed pelvic ligaments let the bones shift slightly, creating a bit more space for the baby to move safely through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: Which specialized structure inside the ventricles makes cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: Dural venous sinus
options.B: Arachnoid granulations
options.C: Choroid plexus
options.D: Cerebral cortex

explanation: Brilliant! The choroid plexus is like a tiny, hardworking sponge network inside the ventricles that constantly produces fresh cerebrospinal fluid. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a must-have before launching any new health program in a community?

options.A: Immediate international funding approval
options.B: Completion of the final program evaluation report
options.C: Permanent replacement of all local health staff
options.D: Community readiness and willingness to participate

explanation: If the community isn't ready or interested, even the best health plan won't work. Always get the people on board first! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h2)

question: What happens immediately to your body when stress hormones like adrenaline rush into your bloodstream?

options.A: Digestion speeds up and saliva increases
options.B: Blood vessels in the muscles constrict
options.C: Heart rate and blood pressure increase
options.D: Pupils constrict to focus on close objects

explanation: Adrenaline gets you ready for action! Your heart pumps faster, blood pressure goes up, and your body preps you to run or fight. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h2)
